title: Willoughbyland founded
description: Barbadian planters sent by the governor of Barbados start sugar estates on the Suriname River, the colony's first English settlement.

title: Treaty of Breda
description: The Dutch keep Suriname and the English keep New Amsterdam (New York), fixing the colony's fate.

title: Society of Suriname chartered
description: The chartered Society of Suriname takes over the colony's plantations, deepening its dependence on slavery and sugar.

title: Treaty with the Maroons
description: The planters sign a peace with the Ndyuka, escaped slaves whose fortresses the army could not reduce, recognising their freedom.

title: British occupy the colony
description: Britain seizes the colony after France absorbs the Netherlands; apart from a brief return the Dutch get it back only at the 1816 restoration.

title: Paramaribo fire
description: A second great fire in eleven years destroys much of the capital, prompting stone building codes.

title: Slavery abolished
description: The Netherlands frees the slaves of Suriname, among the last slaveholders in the Americas, later marked by Keti Koti day.

title: First Indian contract workers
description: The ship Lalla Rookh lands 399 indentured Indians, beginning the migration that makes Hindostanen the largest group.

title: First Javanese arrive
description: The first indentured workers from Java land, adding the group from which Suriname takes its distinctive Javanese culture.

title: American troops arrive
description: US soldiers garrison the colony to guard its bauxite mines, the lifeline of the Allied aluminium industry.

title: Kingdom Charter
description: The Charter for the Kingdom makes Suriname an autonomous country within the Dutch realm with full internal self-government.

title: Independence
description: Suriname becomes an independent republic as a third of the population emigrates to the Netherlands.

title: Sergeants' Coup
description: Sixteen NCOs under Dési Bouterse overthrow the government, beginning over four decades of military and coup-era politics.

title: December murders
description: Fifteen critics of the regime are tortured and shot after a failed counter-coup; the victims become the country's emblem of dictatorship.

title: Interior War
description: The Jungle Commando's fight with the army devastates the Maroon interior; peace is signed in 1992.

title: New constitution
description: A constitutional referendum restores elected government, though the army keeps its veto on power.

title: Bouterse elected president
description: The 1980 coup leader returns, this time as elected president.

title: Bouterse convicted
description: A court finds the former president guilty of murder over the December killings and sentences him in his absence.
